title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 127
paragraphs: So when the Median army had been shamefully dispersed, as soon as Astyages heard of it he said, threatening Cyrus: “Even so, Cyrus shall not escape punishment.” Having spoken thus, he first impaled the Magian interpreters of dreams who had persuaded him to let Cyrus go, and then he armed those Medes, youths and old men, who had been left behind in the city. These he led out, and having engaged in battle with the Persians, he was defeated, and Astyages himself was taken alive, and he also lost the Medes whom he had led forth.
